# NOTES ON THE FIVE-BOOK ANTHOLOGY (for later lookup, not commentary)

## BOOK 1: "When Freemen Shall Stand" (Nelson S. Bond, Fantastic Adventures Nov. 1943)
**Premise/Frame:** Earth conquered by Venus (Daan/Daans). Army lieutenant **Stephen (Steve) Duane**, chemical engineer, and lab assistant **Chuck Lafferty** (calls Steve "Lootenant"), plus Nazi spy **Eric von Rath** (guttural accent, ray pistol, calls Steve "Leutnant"/"Herr"), in a lab test of anesthetic gas **methioprane** (basic ingredient: seed-pod of swamp-musk, a rare tank-epiphyte). Flask breaks; all three cataleptic ~1500 years. Set in 1942 → wakened in 3548 (year "Three-Four-and-Eight-Eight"), in Fort Knox ("Fautnox"), Kentucky, guarded by Mother Maatha of the Tucki Clan and priestess **Beth** (dust-gold hair, steel-blue eyes). Women's matriarchy; males are breeders or "Wild Ones" (Jon, leader). Mount Rushmore = "Place of the Gods" in "'Kota" (Dakota) with "Jarg, Taamuz, Ibrim, Tedhi" (Jefferson/Washington/Lincoln/Roosevelt-like faces). Venus = "Daan"; Daans have webbed hands, pale/silver-haired, rule from **Sinnaty** (Cincinnati; fortress "Nedlunplaza" = Netherland Plaza; Carew Tower). Steve impersonates "Captain Huumo" (via surgeon Okuno/Wiam of Kleevlun, altered earthman). Loovil (Louisville) battle; Steve's ploy: "Trojan horse." Lady **Loala** (silver hair, Overlord) treats Steve with "Treatment" (brain-pattern cylinder; destruction kills). Brotherhood/Fifth Column; Rodrik of Mish-kin (rival, dies when Okuno swaps cylinder). Steve loved Beth; Loala dies after von Rath shot. Steve's crew uses methioprane (distilled from klaar) to put Daan fleet to sleep; Earth regains freedom; ends with Beth: "the flag shall fly again"; final line "For a woman always has the last word."

## BOOK 2: *A Bid for Fortune; or, Dr. Nikola's Vendetta* (Guy Boothby, 1918 ed.)
**Prologue:** Imperial Restaurant, Thames Embankment; manager **McPherson**, bookkeeper **Miss O'Sullivan**. Dinner No. 22 (8 p.m.). Guests: **Eastover** (American, "Nashville"), **Prendergast** (pitted-face, snow-white hair), **Baxter** (clergyman, tutor). Host **Dr. Nikola**: slim, olive skin, black hair, black cat (uncanny), basket. Nikola orders Eastover to Sydney, Prendergast to Paris/Charing Cross, Baxter to tutor the young **Marquis of Beckenham** (son of **Duke of Glenbarth**) at Bournemouth. Target: rich **Wetherell**. Nikola's "Green Sailor" public-house, East India Dock Road.
**Ch I:** Narrator **Richard (Dick) Hatteras**, pearler of Thursday Island, 28; father Englishman, mother died Philippines; schooner *Helen of Troy* lost. Met in Sydney Hon. **Phyllis Wetherell** (daughter of Colonial Secretary **Sylvester Wetherell**, Potts Point) rescued from larrikins in Domain; swindler **Dorunda Dodson** rebuffed. Sails on *Orizaba*; Wetherell forbids romance; they're engaged at Naples sea-shore; he warns she must not marry him.
**Ch II-III:** London: hotel near Strand; rendezvous at British Museum; Nikola reads cards in pocket (Braithwaite, Wetherell, Hatteras) and "burns" fly-paper vision of Phyllis crying "Dick! come to me!" Wetherells flee suddenly. Hampshire, New Forest: Hatteras's father's home **Murdlestone**, uncle **Sir William Hatteras** (miserly; daughter **Gwendoline**, idiot-like). Catullus book evidence. Rejected loan.
**Ch IV-V:** Yacht *Enchantress* at Bournemouth; saves Marquis of Beckenham from drowning; Baxter appears; Duke of Glenbarth visits; Telegram "Nineveh" message "THE TRAIN IS LAID" discovered.
**Ch VI-VII:** Meets Nikola in Green Sailor; Nikola hypnotises; reading of Phyllis's letter from Port Said re Prendergast. Hatteras boards *Saratoga* at Plymouth; drugged; Port Said captivity with Beckenham (mouse-messenger letters), escape.
**Ch VIII-IX:** Marquis and Hatteras chained; Nikola's cat; Nikola's "free passage"; Hatteras learns Baxter used Beckenham's identity; they take *Pescadore* to Melbourne.
**Part II:** Sydney, *General Officer* hotel; false Beckenham at Government House; Mr. Wetherell's sick-bed; **Thompson** coachman drugged at *Canary Bird*; Mr. Draper's house (Charlemagne St.); schooner *Merry Duchess*; Pipa Lannu island; Nikola's note; Phyllis rescued; Hatteras inherits baronetcy (Murdlestone, 15,000 a year); marries Phyllis; Nikola sends diamond collet with card "Dr. Nikola."

## BOOK 3: *Pharos, the Egyptian* (Guy Boothby, 1899)
**Preface:** letter from Sir William Betford (Bampton St. Mary, Dorset) to George Trevelyan (Lincoln's Inn Fields). Cyril Forrester's manuscript; visitor **Honoré de Silva** (agent of Forrester; Asiatic type) delivers packet.
**Ch I:** Forrester, painter, 1 year after Academy picture *Merenptah*. Cleopatra's Needle: Pharos (old, pitted, fur coat, skullcap, monkey **Pehtes**) refuses to rescue drowning man; attacks. Lady Medenham's "at home" → Valerie de Vocsqal (Hungarian violinist, Fräulein; ward of Pharos). 
**Ch II-IV:** Forrester studio (Egyptian decorations; father's mummy-case of **Ptahmes**, Chief of King's Magicians, Pharaoh of Exodus); Pharos hypnotises Forrester, steals mummy. Murder of curiosity dealer **Clausand** in Bonwell Street; suspect **Johann Schmidt** suicide. Sir George Legrath (Egyptian Museum director): "may God help you."
**Ch V-VII:** Naples; Angelotti the letter-writer; Pompeii Temple of Mercury; Tullus Agrippa's house; Pharos's Naples palace; cigarettes drug; Pharos proposes Egypt trip.
**Ch VIII-XI:** Yacht; Valerie warns; Cairo, Pyramid (Queen's Chamber), Sphinx vision; Luxor; Temple of Ammon mummy-ritual; Pehtes; Forrester's fever; Arab dies.
**Ch XII-XVIII:** Prague (Teyn Kirche), Valerie's escape with Forrester; Berlin (Schuncke); Hamburg (plague, Dittmer chemist, Wisemann's ship *Margrave of Brandenburg*); England (Tebworth); Tollingtower house, Park Lane.
**Ch XIX-XXI:** Pharos's plague-spreading; Forrester tells Home Secretary Sir Edward Grangerfield; Pharos hangs/dies; Valerie with Forrester in St James's Park; ends "THE END." Pharos = Ptahmes.

## BOOK 4: *The Red Rat's Daughter* (Guy Boothby, 1899)
**Ch I (narrator-ish):** **John Grantham Browne** (millionaire, soap "Browne's Mimosa Soap"), steam-yacht *Lotus Blossom* (1200 tons). Guests: Duchess of Matlock, Ladies Iseult & Imogen, Miss Verney, Dobson, Barrington-Marsh, Jimmy Foote, Felix Maas. At Merok (Geiranger Fjord) Browne rescues **Katherine Petrovitch** on mountain-side; carries her; his card: "I am Browne's Mimosa Soap."
**Ch II:** Maas: "Marriage." Browne fancies Russia (Demetrovitch). Madame **Bernstein** (guardian, Russian, Hungarian-born), Katherine's home in Warsaw.
**Ch III-IV:** London studio at German Park Road, Melbury Road, Kensington; Pall Mall, Foote; picture of Merok; Katherine's Russian name "Polowski" revealed later; Katherine paints in London.
**Ch V-VI:** Lallemand's dinner; Lohengrin at Covent Garden; Madame's wiles; Paris; Rue Jacquarie 35.
**Ch VII-XII:** Katherine's father **Stefan Polowski** (Nihilist, Siberia, Saghalien); Madame Bernstein = Red Rat's wife? (Revealed later: Red Rat = Kleinkopf, diamond-thief; Madame's husband).
**Ch XIII-XIV:** Otto Sauber (old patriot); Hong-kong contact **Johann Schmidt**.
**Ch XV-XXIII:** Browne buys ring; Maas invites self; Captain Mason (Lotus Blossom); MacAndrew (ex-Oxford, rescue planner, £5000 in gold); Saghalien rescue in Bay of Kroptskoi; Russian cruiser; Maas drugged and sent to Tomari (Kunashiri).
**Ch XXIV-XXX:** Japan, Yokohama; Katherine; Madame; MacAndrew reveals: convict = Red Rat (Kleinkopf, Madame's husband), real Polowski dead early last year; Katherine's father never rescued; Maas betrayed them; Browne/Katherine end: "you are not THE RED RAT'S DAUGHTER!"

## BOOK 5: *The Fatal Three* (M. E. Braddon, 3 vols, 1880s; three Gutenberg vols, combined here)
**Vol I. Book I "Clotho; or Spinning the Thread."** Mr. John Fausset (wealthy, ex-wholesale silk, Lyons), wife **Maud (Donfrey)** daughter of Lord Castle-Connell; daughter **Mildred** (7). Ward **Fay** (14, dark hair, "Fay Fausset"), sent to Brussels finishing school after Bell reports; Bell (Martha Bell, Maud's nurse, Irish; Patrick Bell husband). Upper Parchment Street (London), The Hook (Chertsey–Windsor river villa). Mildred & Fay bond; Mildred's scarlet fever; Fay's "sister" comment; Maud: "The girl is his natural daughter." Mildred's mother dies later.
**Ch V-VIII:** George Greswold (Ransome, Enderby Manor, Hampshire; Lola's child, Mildred's daughter Lola (12) dies of typhoid from polluted garden-well water, dairy-woman Mrs. Wadman); Mildred marries Greswold. Castellani (César, Milanese, author of *Nepenthe*, singer/pianist) arrives at Enderby; mentions Greswold's first wife (Vivien Faux; "Fay"). Clergyman **Clement Cancellor** (St Elizabeth's, Parchment Street).
**Ch IX-XIII:** Mildred's realisation Greswold's first wife = Fay; she leaves Enderby, goes to Brighton (aunt **Gertrude Fausset**, Lewes Crescent, Miss Fausset, Vicar Maltravers). Pamela Ransome (niece, 15 years?; Box the terrier).
**Ch XIV-XVIII (Vol I end):** Mildred confronts Greswold; he reveals first marriage (Vivien Faux, married Florence 1868; she died at Nice (St Jean) 24 April 1868 by cliff fall). Mildred's photograph discovery.

**Vol II. Book II "Lachesis; or the Meter of Destiny."** Greswold's letter; Bell confirms Fay's paternity; solicitors Pergament; Mildred to Brighton; Miss Fausset's confessions of hard heart; Castellani attempts Mildred; Pamela & Castellani; Mildred and Pamela to Pallanza (Italy); Nice; Lady Lochinvar; Maria Castellani at madhouse (Castellani's cousin, prima donna); Mildred visits Le Bout du Monde (St Jean) and graves; Greswold alone.
**Vol II ends:** Mildred back at Brighton; Castellani's accusations (George Ransome was "a murderer and madman"); Mildred's journey.

**Vol III. Book III "Atropos; or That Which Must Be."** Ransome's history: marriage to Vivien (Fay) at Florence (Vivien Faux, Mortimers), Nice; Fay's suicide over cliff at St Jean after quarrel; Ransome in asylum; mother's death; reunion with Mildred; Miss Fausset reveals she herself was Castellani's victim (Milan, mock marriage to Paolo Castellani, bore Fay—Fanny Fausset/Fay natural daughter of John Fausset's sister Gertrude); letters found by Mildred at The Hook; Mildred returns to Enderby; Pamela marries Malcolm Stuart (Lady Lochinvar's nephew) at Westminster Abbey; Miss Fausset dies; Mildred inherits; Greswold Hospital founded; Castellani fades. End: "THE END."
